# BAD-051 — One comment-and-type pass over server/supabase/functions/: stale admin pointers, cross-file above/below references, room.ts's spread claim, and deno check's three TS7006s

## Brief
One pass over `server/supabase/functions/`, because every edit here redeploys: `server-deploy.yml` applies migrations and deploys Edge Functions on merge to `main`, so four separate comment-and-type PRs would be four deploys for changes that alter no behaviour at all. Merged from BAD-051, BAD-075 and BAD-082 (2026-09-16 triage) and BAD-088 (2026-09-16 nightly triage); each was filed separately as the out-of-scope tail of a different split, and each is mechanical.

Three deliverables, all verified present on main e9f8709:

**1. Line-number pointers into the admin, now stale (was BAD-051).** `server/supabase/functions/account/index.ts` cites `admin/src/lib/actions.ts:216` (line 23) and `admin/src/lib/actions.ts:363-366` (line 57). BAD-053 split that file: `admin/src/lib/actions.ts` is now a 17-line barrel and those functions live in `admin/src/lib/actions/accounts.ts`. Name the symbols instead of the lines — `deleteAccount`'s typed confirmation, `deleteAuthUser`'s exact-address re-check — so the next split cannot break them again. The same pointers are copied in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-09-account-deletion.md:672,692`; that is a historical plan, leave it.

**2. `above`/`below` references that now cross files (was BAD-075).** BAD-047's PR 2 was a pure move, so every comment inside a moved block travelled byte-for-byte — and several navigate by position in a file that no longer holds what they point at. Confirmed on main: `lifecycle.ts:65` says the guarded UPDATE works "exactly like the commit path's fallback stamp below", which is now `push.ts` (`commitUpload`'s isHost-guarded UPDATE), while what is actually below it in `lifecycle.ts` is `wrapRoom`. `push.ts:190` says "the gun itself is the host's Start (mode 'start' above)", which is `lifecycle.ts`'s `startRoom`. `room.ts:93` calls the phase-aware expiry "shared by every gate below", and the gates are now spread over six sibling files.

Leave these alone — their referent moved with them and they still read correctly: `room.ts:20`, `room.ts:54`, `info.ts:108`, `lifecycle.ts:146`, `pull.ts:15` ("sits below the membership gate", still true of the dispatch order), `gate.ts:2`, `bucket.ts:3,28,41`, `index.ts:66,69,119-120`, `sweep.ts:52`.

**3. `deno check`'s entire error set (was BAD-082).** `server/supabase/functions/collab/info.ts` has three TS7006 implicit-any map parameters and nothing else: `members.map((m) => ...)`, `claims.map((c) => ...)`, `takes.map((t) => ...)`. Each reports `TS7006 [ERROR]: Parameter 'm'/'c'/'t' implicitly has an 'any' type`. Neighbouring code already annotates the same shape — `browse.ts:62` writes `rows.filter((r: any) => listableCollab(r))`. Out of scope for BAD-068, which was told explicitly not to fix them. Clearing these makes `deno check` a clean baseline, which BAD-047's spike §8a leans on.

Not in scope: `push.ts:9` names the duplicated wrap rule ("the SECOND copy"). That is BAD-038's job, not a comment fix — leave the comment until BAD-038 removes the thing it describes.

**4. `room.ts`'s spread claim is wrong about its own mechanism (was BAD-088).** The `Room.collab` comment (`server/supabase/functions/collab/room.ts:22-24` on main 386ae63, reworded but not corrected by BAD-038) still says a spread copy "would hand it the pre-wrap phase with no type error to say so". It would not. `Object.assign(collab, done)` runs at `room.ts:79`, well before the return, so a spread taken on the return line copies the ALREADY-wrapped status: identity and spread give info the same phase. The property the comment defends — hand back the row by identity — is real and correct; the mechanism it gives for why is not, and a reader who trusts it guards against a harmless edit while missing the one that would actually break the wrap-on-read: a copy taken BEFORE the wrap block, or a refactor that makes the wrap write to something other than the object that is returned. Correct the reason, keep the rule. Confirmed: `Object.assign` is the only mutation of `collab` in the whole tree (one hit, `room.ts:79`); readers are `info.ts:47` (`status`) and `info.ts:50` (`phase`). The same sentence is repeated in the BAD-047 commit message (c6b41a9) and in `test/fixtures/movecheck/bad-047-collab.json`'s loadRoom-return group reason; those are historical records, leave them — fixing the source comment is the fix.

Verification: `deno check` on the touched functions ends with zero errors; `npm test` for anything that reads these files. No behaviour changes, so no smoke leg applies.
